panels.title: What did it cost — in tokens
Total tokens

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.input_tokens + s.output_tokens
       + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0) + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Every token billed: uncached input + cache reads + cache writes + output.

**Almost all of it is cache reads.** Measured here: 7.53B cache reads, 54.6M cache writes, 13.2M uncached input, 7.9M output — so this number tracks how much context was re-sent, not how much the models produced. The four tiles to the right hold the same breakdown as live figures.

Tokens, not currency: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so a price table would report money nobody spent. Multiply by your own contract if you need a figure.

panels.title: Output tokens

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.output_tokens), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.output_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
What the models actually produced, as opposed to what was re-sent to them.

Typically a fraction of a percent of the total — 0.1% measured here.

**Total and Output are three orders of magnitude apart**, so they render in different units (B against M) and comparing them by eye reads as a contradiction. They are not: 7.6 B is a thousand times 7.6 M.

panels.title: Uncached input

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.input_tokens), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Input the model had to read fresh, at full price.

This is the figure a cache is meant to shrink. It was missing from this dashboard entirely, which left the headline total — almost all of it cache reads — looking like the whole story.

panels.title: Cache reads

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.cache_read_tokens), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.cache_read_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Context re-sent and served from cache at about a tenth of base rate.

Normally the largest number on this dashboard by three orders of magnitude — 99% of the total here — which is why the headline figure is not a measure of how much work was produced.

panels.title: Served from cache

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))
  / NULLIF(SUM(s.input_tokens + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0)
             + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)), 0), 1) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Share of input tokens served from cache.

**Cache writes count as uncached here**, because a write arrives uncached and is billed above base rate. Omitting them turns a real 48% into a flattering 99% — measured on this project's own data.

panels.title: Cache write payback

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))
  / NULLIF(SUM(s.cache_write_tokens), 0), 2) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.cache_write_tokens IS NOT NULL AND s.cache_write_tokens > 0 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Reads returned per token written to cache — a **ratio, not a percentage**. 135 means each cached token was read back 135 times.

Below 1.25x the writes cost more than they saved — a write is billed at about 1.25x base and a read at 0.1x.

**The obvious break-even of 1.0 is wrong**: a series at 1.10x lost money while looking healthy.

Empty for Codex, which reports cache reads but never writes.

panels.title: Context pressure — the part you can act on
Reasoning tokens

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.reasoning_tokens), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.reasoning_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Tokens spent thinking rather than answering.

Codex alone reports this. Claude Code and Antigravity do not separate it, so an empty panel here means 'not reported', not zero.

panels.title: Human edited the agent's output

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN e.user_modified = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS v
FROM whodunit_events e
WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  e.user_modified IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR e.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Share of edits a human changed before committing — the difference between 'the agent wrote this' and 'the agent wrote this and it was kept'.

Claude Code alone reports it. The denominator counts only calls that carried the signal, so agents without it do not dilute the rate.

panels.title: Turn latency

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.duration_ms) / 1000, 1) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.duration_ms IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: Codex alone records per-turn timing. Claude Code and Antigravity report none, so this is empty for them rather than zero — a zero would make them the fastest agents on this panel.

panels.title: Sessions that compacted

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.compactions > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.compactions IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Share of sessions whose context was compacted at least once (NAV-106).

**Read this beside the context the sessions were running at.** A long session costs more even when cached, because the whole context is re-sent every turn — and compacting is the one thing a person can do about it. Measured on this machine, 92% of turns ran above 150k context while a small fraction of sessions ever compacted.

**Deliberately not colour-coded.** A low rate is only a problem alongside high context, and this panel cannot see context — a short session has nothing to compact, and colouring 8% red would call that a failure. The number is the finding; the judgement needs the context distribution, which the journal cannot answer per turn yet.

The denominator counts only sessions from agents that report the signal at all. Antigravity has no equivalent and is excluded rather than counted as never compacting.

panels.title: Compact rate by agent

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.agent AS metric,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.compactions > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)) AS value
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.compactions IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY s.agent ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.description:
The same rate split by agent — the cut that says whether this is a habit or a tool difference.

Measured here: Claude Code 15% against Codex 4%, on the same repositories and the same person. A gap that size is more likely about how each agent surfaces the option than about who was using it.

Antigravity is absent rather than shown at 0%: it records no context management, so it cannot report a rate at all (NAV-21).

panels.title: Compactions per compacting session

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.compactions), 1) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.compactions > 0 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description:
Average compactions, counting only sessions that compacted at all.

The zeroes are excluded deliberately. Averaged over every session this would be a fraction and would say nothing; the question is what a compacting session looks like — measured here, 4 on average, with one session reaching 9.

A high number is not automatically bad: it means long work, which is sometimes exactly right.

panels.title: Reasoning effort

targets.rawSql:
SELECT s.effort AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.effort IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY s.effort

defaults.noValue: no session recorded an effort tier

panels.description:
How hard the model was asked to think, where the agent says.

The lever behind the token counts above: a higher tier spends more on the same task.

panels.title: Per model — where the aggregate hides a loss
Token mix by model

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(s.model, ''), '(unattributed)') AS model,
  SUM(s.input_tokens)                             AS `Uncached in`,
  SUM(s.output_tokens)                            AS `Output`,
  SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0))           AS `Cache write`,
  SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))            AS `Cache read`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY SUM(s.input_tokens + s.output_tokens
           + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0)
           + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)) DESC

panels.description:
What each model's tokens are made of — one stacked bar per model.

**Stacked as a percentage, not as absolute counts, and that is the only way this reads.** Cache reads are 88-99% of every model's total here, so an absolute stack would draw one long bar with three invisible slivers: opus-5's entire output is 0.1% of its own total. Normalising each bar to 100% makes the composition comparable, which is where the difference actually is — gpt-5.4 is 94% cache reads against gpt-5.5 at 88%.

Absolute totals are in the table below; this panel answers what the tokens were, not how many.

Ordered by total tokens, so the largest consumer is at the top even though every bar is the same length.

panels.title: Longest sessions

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (s.last_seen - s.first_seen) DESC),
    '. ', s.agent, ' · ',
    COALESCE(NULLIF(s.model, ''), 'model not reported')) AS metric,
  ROUND((s.last_seen - s.first_seen) / 1000000000 / 3600, 1) AS value
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND s.last_seen > s.first_seen
  -- A session whose first record predates the ingest window carries the
  -- zero time, which reaches the database as -6795364578871345152 and
  -- renders as a 272-year session. The adapter no longer writes those,
  -- but a database synced before that fix still holds them, and one such
  -- row at the top of a DESC sort makes the whole panel nonsense.
  AND s.first_seen > 0
ORDER BY (s.last_seen - s.first_seen) DESC LIMIT 8

defaults.noValue: no sessions with a usable duration

panels.description:
The eight longest sessions, in hours. A long session costs more even when cached, because the whole context is re-sent every turn.

Individual sessions rather than an average, deliberately: the mean here is a few hours and the top session is 339, so an average would hide exactly the ones worth looking at.

**Rows are numbered because the labels repeat.** Several of the longest sessions are the same agent with no model recorded, and a bar gauge needs distinct labels or it silently collapses them into one bar.

Sessions whose start time was never recorded are excluded rather than rendered as impossibly long.

panels.title: Token use and cache efficiency by model

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(s.model, ''), '(unattributed)') AS Model,
  COUNT(*)                                        AS Sessions,
  SUM(s.input_tokens)                             AS `Uncached in`,
  SUM(s.output_tokens)                            AS `Out`,
  SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))            AS `Cache read`,
  SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0))           AS `Cache write`,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))
    / NULLIF(SUM(s.input_tokens + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0)
               + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)), 0), 1) AS `From cache %`,
  ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0))
    / NULLIF(SUM(s.cache_write_tokens), 0), 1)    AS `Write payback ×`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(s.model, ''), '(unattributed)')
ORDER BY SUM(s.input_tokens + s.output_tokens
           + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0)
           + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)) DESC

panels.description:
**Per model, because the aggregate hides the finding.** An overall 48% read ratio measured on real data contained one model at 0.73x amortisation — a loss, invisible in the total.

`Write payback` below 1.25x is red: those writes cost more than they saved. Empty means the agent does not report cache writes rather than that it wrote none.

panels.title: Output tokens per model over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(s.last_seen / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(s.model, ''), '(unattributed)')                AS metric,
  SUM(s.output_tokens)                                           AS value
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.output_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND s.last_seen >= $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
  AND s.last_seen <  $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.description:
Which model is doing the work, and when that changed.

One line per model, named and coloured. That needs `format: time_series`, which is what turns a `metric` column into separate series — with `format: table` Grafana returns one frame with a literal metric column and labels every line "value", so the models are indistinguishable.

Full width because the cache-payback chart that used to sit beside it was removed: payback is a static per-model fact here, not a trend. Three of seven models never report cache writes at all and the rest sit at 47-153x, so plotting it over time drew four flat lines nowhere near the break-even the chart existed to mark. The number itself stays in the table below, where its session count is beside it — 153x reads very differently on 34 sessions than on 1.

panels.title: Top agent-written lines by branch

targets.rawSql:
SELECT branch, `Lines added` FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN CHAR_LENGTH(e.branch) > 34
         THEN CONCAT(LEFT(e.branch, 31), '...')
         ELSE e.branch END      AS branch,
    SUM(e.lines_added)          AS `Lines added`,
    1                           AS grp,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(e.lines_added) DESC) AS rn
  FROM whodunit_events e
  WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  e.branch IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR e.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  GROUP BY e.branch
  HAVING SUM(e.lines_added) > 0
) ranked WHERE rn <= 12
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CONCAT('+ ', COUNT(*), ' more branches'),
  SUM(lines_added)
FROM (
  SELECT
    SUM(e.lines_added) AS lines_added,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(e.lines_added) DESC) AS rn
  FROM whodunit_events e
  WHERE e.branch IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR e.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  GROUP BY e.branch
  HAVING SUM(e.lines_added) > 0
) tail WHERE rn > 12
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.description:
Where the agent's output actually landed, top twelve branches by lines written, with everything below them summed into a final bar.

That last bar is there so the top twelve reads as a slice rather than as everything — the failure the old table's silent LIMIT 25 already caused once. Measured here the twelve are 90% of all lines written across 42 branches.

Branches contributing zero lines are excluded — those are sessions that read and ran things without writing, which the events count already covers elsewhere.

Long branch names are truncated for the axis; the tooltip carries the value and the panel beside this one says how much sits outside the top twelve.

Antigravity records no branch at all — its branch-like strings are a tracker's *suggested* branch inside an MCP response, not the checked-out one. Its events are absent here rather than grouped under a wrong name.

panels.title: MCP servers, and how much rope the agent had
Autonomy granted — tool calls per session

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(s.permission_mode, '  (', s.agent, ')')  AS metric,
  ROUND(SUM(s.tool_calls) / COUNT(*))              AS value
FROM whodunit_sessions s
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  s.permission_mode IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR s.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY s.permission_mode, s.agent
ORDER BY 2 DESC

defaults.noValue: no session recorded a permission mode

panels.description:
How much work happens per session at each level of autonomy.

**One metric rather than two bars.** Sessions and total tool calls run in opposite directions here — 64 sessions on Codex's `never` produced 506 calls, 2 Claude Code sessions on `auto` produced 6,766 — so charting both put a 13x range beside a 32x one and flattened whichever shared the axis. Dividing them gives the thing both were circling: 8 calls per session on `never`, 3,383 on `auto`.

The ladder is monotonic across every mode measured, which is the finding: autonomy is not how often it is granted, it is how much happens once it is.

The agent is in the label because each mode belongs to exactly one — Codex says `never` and `on-request`, Claude Code says `acceptEdits`, `auto` and `default`. Each agent's own vocabulary is kept rather than mapped onto a shared enum: asserting that `never` means the same as `default` would invent a comparison neither agent made.

panels.title: Calls per MCP server

targets.rawSql:
SELECT e.mcp_server AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value
FROM whodunit_events e
WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND  e.mcp_server IS NOT NULL AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR e.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY e.mcp_server ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 15

panels.description:
Which servers the agents actually reach for.

Antigravity is absent: what looked like MCP identity in its store turned out to be the command text being approved, which is content rather than an identifier.
